product: Deepgram — speech to text, streaming (Live Audio WebSocket)

source_audio.description: No audio was submitted and no request was issued: this frame is authored to Deepgram's published streaming-protocol documentation, not captured from the service. The Metadata message carries no transcript, so no spoken or written content is involved at all.

redaction.notes: Nothing was redacted because nothing was captured. request_id holds the nil GUID and the audio digest field holds an all-zero 64-hex fill — the placeholder forms protocol section 4 prescribes — because no real request or audio stream exists to identify.

terms.basis: docs/guides/provider-recording-protocol.md section 7 — Deepgram is not-cleared for capturing Output, so this fixture takes the documentation-derived route, which contains no Output at all

source_schema.method: The documented field set of the streaming Metadata message was read from the page above: type, transaction_key, request_id, sha256, created, duration, channels. No vendor example payload, prose or field description was copied — only the documented field names, the literal message-type constant 'Metadata' and the documented transaction_key sentinel, both of which are interface constants rather than expression. Every other value is our own fiction.

notes: The non-Results control frame. DeepgramSpeechRecognizer filters on type != "Results" and this fixture is what makes that filter assertable: before it, no test in the suite ever sent the parser a frame it was supposed to ignore. What this artifact is worth, stated plainly: a documented schema is what the vendor says it sends, whereas a capture is what it actually sent on one day. This route closes the field-set and frame-ordering half of the ADR-0041 D4 gap and cannot close the does-the-vendor-honour-its-own-docs half. Re-read the source_schema URL first when this suite starts failing; the page publishes no revision marker, so a silent breaking edit is indistinguishable from no edit at all.
